displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest realist case treats objective normative facts as the best component of a holistic explanation of deliberative authority, counterfactual stability, and justified normative correction.

novelty.explanation: This steelman repairs the undeveloped comparative claim by identifying specific phenomena and framing realism as an abductive conclusion.

premises.text: Deliberation presents some considerations as reasons whose authority is not exhausted by an agent's present desires, endorsements, or social conventions.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's vindication claim by specifying authority within practical and epistemic deliberation.

premises.text: Counterfactual moral judgments remain intelligible when speakers imagine altered collective attitudes, suggesting that attitude variation and correctness conditions perform distinguishable roles.

novelty.explanation: This develops the linguistic pressure without treating accommodation of the phenomenon as an immediate realist concession.

premises.text: A genealogy defeats normative belief only when evidence connects its causal mechanism to unreliability; cultural variation or localized membership alone cannot supply that connection.

novelty.explanation: This combines the belief-fact distinction with the transcript's explicit threshold for genuine debunking evidence.

premises.text: A fair comparison should count realism's ontology against any semantic, psychological, and pragmatic machinery rivals require to preserve deliberation, disagreement, and correction.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the vague cost comparison by requiring symmetric accounting across explicit explanatory dimensions.

conclusion.text: If realism explains these phenomena more comprehensively under symmetric cost accounting, objective normative facts are provisionally warranted despite continuing epistemological and ontological objections.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion makes the realist result conditional and proportionate, repairing the transcript's comparatively overstated cost claim.

newArguments.title: Normative error without endorsement
newArguments.text: Practices of moral correction distinguish changing someone's attitudes from showing those attitudes mistaken. A purely attitude-dependent account can reproduce the social act of correction, but it must explain why participants regard improved information and consistency as revealing error rather than merely producing new preferences. Realism offers a direct interpretation: correction aims, however imperfectly, at reasons that are not constituted by the corrected person's former endorsement. This does not prove realism, but it adds a specific phenomenon to the holistic comparison.

novelty.explanation: This is a new reinforcing line based on the distinction between causal attitude change and correction represented as discovering error.

newArguments.title: Symmetric theoretical accounting
newArguments.text: Ontological parsimony should not be evaluated independently of explanatory complexity. An anti-realist theory may posit fewer kinds of facts yet require elaborate semantic, pragmatic, and psychological resources to explain disagreement, counterfactual stability, and deliberative authority. Conversely, realism must count its epistemology and metaphysics openly. A theory-by-theory ledger comparing common phenomena, auxiliary commitments, and residual problems would convert the transcript's informal plausibility points into a transparent method and prevent either side from receiving cost-free explanatory machinery.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the explicit comparative procedure missing from the live claim that realism has lower cumulative costs.

thesis.text: The strongest anti-realist case holds that objective normative facts are unwarranted unless they add explanatory power beyond empirically grounded accounts of moral psychology, language, and social regulation.

novelty.explanation: This steelman repairs the asserted superfluity claim by making it a conditional explanatory challenge rather than a completed result.

premises.text: Ordinary speakers can condemn conduct, deliberate seriously, and express counterfactual commitments without possessing any determinate implicit theory about mind-independent normative facts.

novelty.explanation: This combines metaethical neutrality with the distinction between first-order commitment and second-order interpretation.

premises.text: Meaning-in-use accounts can analyze moral assertions through standards, commitments, communicative intentions, and inferential practices while preserving sincere disagreement as a practical phenomenon.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the deferred linguistic case by identifying concrete explanatory resources rather than merely denying realist priority.

premises.text: Causal explanations of normative belief become epistemically relevant only when a demonstrated mechanism predicts error or insensitivity, not merely because believers form a minority.

novelty.explanation: This accepts the live evidential threshold and repairs the hypothetical genealogy by requiring testable mechanism evidence.

premises.text: If descriptive accounts explain behavior, discourse, deliberation, and correction without objective facts, realism must identify an additional phenomenon that its posit explains distinctively.

novelty.explanation: This converts broad dissolution into a focused comparative burden while preserving the realist's proposed facts-as-data response.

conclusion.text: Absent a demonstrated explanatory remainder uniquely favoring objective normative facts, global normative anti-realism remains a proportionate interpretation of moral and epistemic practice.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion remains conditional upon explanatory comparison and therefore avoids overstating what descriptive coverage alone establishes.

newArguments.title: Intervention-based explanatory test
newArguments.text: Competing metaethical explanations can be compared through intervention. If changes in information, incentives, identity, social coordination, or emotional salience systematically predict changes in moral judgment, descriptive mechanisms gain explanatory support. Realism may still interpret some resulting judgments as more accurate, but it should identify additional predictions or explanatory constraints contributed by objective facts. This test does not assume that causal explanation settles truth; it asks whether the realist posit produces identifiable explanatory value beyond the psychological and social model.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an empirical intervention criterion for comparing explanatory contributions without equating causal explanation with metaphysical refutation.

newArguments.title: Metaethical underdetermination of practice
newArguments.text: The same stable practice can support multiple metaethical interpretations. Speakers may condemn cruelty across counterfactual changes because their evaluative standards are deeply entrenched, because discourse conventionally suppresses perspective parameters, or because they track mind-independent reasons. If these interpretations predict the same ordinary behavior and language, practice alone underdetermines metaphysics. The realist must identify discriminating evidence, while the anti-realist must provide an explicit semantic model. This mutual demand strengthens anti-realism by denying default priority without pretending that compatibility already establishes explanatory equality.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the linguistic argument by distinguishing underdetermination from proof and assigning explicit comparative burdens to both accounts.
